Context/Background: UBE2M, an essential neddylation E2 enzyme, has been implicated in the pathogenesis of various diseases, including cancers, viral infections, and obesity. However, whether UBE2M is involved in the pathogenesis of bacterial sepsis remains unclear. In an Escherichia coli (E. coli)-induced sepsis mouse model, increased UBE2M expression in macrophages in liver and lung tissues postinfection was observed. To further clarify the role of UBE2M in macrophages, mice with macrophage-specific deletion of UBE2M were constructed.
Prompt: We isolated and purified peritoneal macrophages (PMs) from control mice and mice with UBE2M deletion.  We then stimulated PMs with Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) (to mimic infection) and performed RNASeq.  Based on the differential expression analysis between PMS of control (WL) vs UBE2M deletion (KL) mice under LPS stimulation, please provide a discussion of the genes and affected pathways as relates to UBE2M deletion in the context of bacterial sepsis.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Peritoneal macrophages (PMs) were isolated from control (wild-type, WL) and macrophage-specific UBE2M knockout (KL) mice. After LPS stimulation (to mimic Gram-negative infection), RNA-Seq was performed on three biological replicates per group (KL1–3 vs WL1–3). Raw counts (PMC11780929-count.csv) were analyzed by DESeq2 followed by preranked GSEA and over-representation analysis (ORA). Definitive signals: UBE2M deletion in LPS-stimulated PMs led to hyperactivation of inflammatory and cell-cycle programs, with concomitant suppression of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation. For any detail not explicitly provided by the input or tool outputs (e.g., precise replicate numbers beyond the three per group), “not specified.”

Keywords  
• neddylation • inflammation/cytokine signaling • mitochondrial metabolism • cell cycle checkpoints • LPS-induced sepsis

Candidate Genes  
UBE2M, NEDD8, NFKB1, IL6, IL1B, NOS2, STAT3, CCL2

Pathway Enrichments  
Counts by database (up vs down):  
KEGG_2016: 31 up / 28 down (52.5 % up, ratio 1.11)  
GO_Biological_Process_2023: 283 / 90 (75.9 % up, ratio 3.14)  
Reactome_Pathways_2024: 83 / 98 (45.9 % up, ratio 0.85)  
MSigDB_Hallmark_2020: 11 / 10 (52.4 % up, ratio 1.10)

KEGG_2016 (UP):  
| Theme                                | Direction | Leading Genes (selected)                                            |  
|--------------------------------------|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|  
| Cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction | Up        | TNFSF18, CCR4, CSF3R, IL12A, CXCL10, IL6, IL1B, CCL2, CCL5, IFNB1    |  
| Jak-STAT signaling pathway           | Up        | JAK3, STAT4, CSF3R, IL12A, IL6, IL10, SOCS1, SOCS3                   |

| Chagas disease                       | Up        | C1QB, IL12A, NFKB1, IL6, IL10, NOS2                                  |  
| Oxidative phosphorylation            | Down      | NDUFA9, SDHB, COX8A, UQCRC2, SDHA, NDUFS1                           |

|--------------------------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|  
| Inflammatory Response                            | Up        | NFKB1, IL6, NOS2, IL1B, CCL2, CXCL10, TLR2                                          |  
| Mitotic Sister Chromatid Segregation             | Up        | ESPL1, NCAPD2, SMC2, PLK1, AURKB                                                     |  
| Positive Regulation Of Cell Cycle Process        | Up        | MAD2L1, CCNB1, CDC6, BIRC5, AURKA                                                     |  
| Regulation Of Cytokine Production                | Up        | IL6, IL10, NOS2, CCR2, IL1A                                                          |

Reactome_Pathways_2024 (UP):  
| Theme                                               | Direction | Leading Genes (selected)                                  |  
|-----------------------------------------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------|  
| Mitotic Spindle Checkpoint                          | Up        | BUB1, MAD2L1, CCNB1, PLK1, NDC80                          |  
| Amplification of Signal From Unattached Kinetochores | Up        | BUB1, MAD2L1, NDC80, PLK1, AURKB                         |

MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 (UP):  
| Theme                         | Direction | Leading Genes (selected)                            |  
|-------------------------------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------|  
| G2-M Checkpoint               | Up        | CDK1, BUB1, CCNB1, CDC20, UBE2C                      |  
| Interferon Gamma Response     | Up        | STAT1, IRF1, CXCL10, NFKB1, IFNAR2                   |  
| Allograft Rejection           | Up        | IL12A, IL6, CCR2, NOS2, CCL2                         |  
| Inflammatory Response         | Up        | IL1B, IL6, CXCL10, NFKBIA, TLR2                      |  
| E2F Targets                   | Up        | MCM6, CDKN1B, RRM2, E2F2, PLK4                        |

Balancing across libraries: UBE2M deletion drives a strong pro-inflammatory signature (KEGG cytokine/STAT, Hallmark INFγ), coupled with cell-cycle activation (GO mitosis, Hallmark G2-M and E2F targets). By contrast, mitochondrial respiration (KEGG oxidative phosphorylation) is robustly down-regulated, suggesting a metabolic shift to glycolytic/inflammatory metabolism. Reactome shows discordant balance (slightly more down than up), reflecting specific metabolic and surface‐receptor pathways suppressed.

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
Filtered GSEA for “cytokine”:  
• KEGG_2016: Cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction (NES 6.58, lead genes above)  
• GO_BP: Regulation Of Cytokine Production (NES 3.90)  
• GO_BP: Cytokine-Mediated Signaling Pathway (NES 3.82)  
• GO_BP: Response To Cytokine (NES 3.40)  

Filtered GSEA for “oxidative”:  
• KEGG_2016: Oxidative phosphorylation (NES –4.14)  
• GO_BP: Oxidative Phosphorylation (NES –3.47)  
• Hallmark: Oxidative Phosphorylation (NES –4.05)  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading edge)  
Up :  
| Gene  | Direction | Role/Function                 | Pathway(s)                                |  
|-------|-----------|-------------------------------|-------------------------------------------|  
| IL6   | Up        | Proinflammatory cytokine      | Cytokine-cytokine receptor; Jak-STAT; Hallmark Infl. Response |  
| NFKB1 | Up        | NF-κB transcription subunit    | Inflammatory Response; TNF signaling     |  
| IL1B  | Up        | Pyrogenic cytokine            | Cytokine-mediated signaling; KEGG Cytokine |  
| NOS2  | Up        | Nitric oxide production       | Chagas; Inflammatory Response            |  
| CCL2  | Up        | Monocyte chemoattractant      | Cytokine interaction; Hallmark Allograft |  

Down :  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                   | Pathway(s)                         |  
|---------|-----------|---------------------------------|------------------------------------|  
| NDUFA9  | Down      | Complex I subunit, OXPHOS        | Oxidative phosphorylation (KEGG/GO/Hallmark) |  
| SDHB    | Down      | Complex II subunit, TCA cycle    | Oxidative phosphorylation          |  
| COX8A   | Down      | Complex IV subunit               | Hallmark Oxidative Phosphorylation |  
| UQCRC2  | Down      | Complex III subunit              | Oxidative phosphorylation          |  
| SDHA    | Down      | Complex II subunit               | GO OXPHOS                          |  

Comparisons  
Patterns in PMs mirror those seen in sepsis-activated macrophages (Hallmark Inflammatory response) but with exaggerated cell-cycle signatures not typical of terminally differentiated macrophages (lower confidence). Mitochondrial suppression is consistent with Warburg-like switch in inflamed macrophages.

Implications  
UBE2M/neddylation modulates the balance between metabolic and inflammatory programs in macrophages under bacterial challenge. Loss of UBE2M sensitizes cells to pro-inflammatory cytokine production (IL-6, IL-1β) and cell‐cycle entry, while impairing mitochondrial respiration—a dual effect that may exacerbate sepsis pathology by promoting cytokine storm and metabolic dysfunction.

Next Steps & Clarification  
1. Validate key DE genes (IL6, IL1B, NOS2) at protein level in PMs by ELISA/Western blot.  
2. Examine macrophage bioenergetics (Seahorse assay) to confirm OXPHOS suppression upon UBE2M deletion.  
3. Test whether pharmacological neddylation inhibition (MLN4924) recapitulates KL phenotype in wild-type PMs.  
4. Investigate impact on bacterial clearance in vivo—assess bacterial load and survival in UBE2M-deficient mice.

References  
None (no PMIDs directly returned by literature-mining tools).
